objectives: Segment simple w-initial CVC words into phonemes.
Map each phoneme to a grapheme in sequence.
Spell taught w-initial CVC words accurately.
Use dictation, rereading and self-correction to verify spelling.
concepts: Encoding moves from spoken phonemes to written graphemes.
CVC spelling requires all three phonemes to be represented.
The initial /w/ is mapped to w in taught words.
Rereading a written word helps detect omitted or substituted sounds.

definitions.definition: Representing spoken sounds with letters or graphemes to write a word.
Breaking a spoken word into its individual phonemes.
Writing a word or sentence that is spoken aloud.

workedExamples: Say 'wag', segment /w/ /a/ /g/, then read back wag.
commonMistakes: Writing a letter for a sound that was not heard.
Failing to read back the written word.
keyTakeaways: Write one grapheme for each taught sound.

basic: Segment and spell simple w-initial CVC words.
conceptual: Identify the grapheme representing each phoneme in a w-CVC word.
application: Spell fresh w-initial CVC words from dictation.
higherOrderThinking: Explain how rereading reveals a missing phoneme in a spelling attempt.
mixedReview: Mix w-CVC encoding with previously taught CVC spelling patterns.

quickRevision: hear word → segment sounds → map sounds → write → reread
formulaOrFactBank: CVC encoding = phoneme 1 + phoneme 2 + phoneme 3 → graphemes
mistakeBasedRevision: If spelling is wrong, say the word slowly and identify the missing or changed phoneme.
weakTopicRevision: Practise the vowel or final consonant that is repeatedly omitted or substituted.

activities.name: Sound-to-letter mapping
steps: Write one grapheme for each sound.

activities.name: Dictation and repair
steps: Correct any missing or changed sound.

outcomes: Learner segments w-initial CVC words into three phonemes.
Learner maps each phoneme to an appropriate taught grapheme.
Learner spells dictated w-CVC words and self-corrects errors.
